parsed.explanation: Combined regime: no criminalisation of same-sex conduct and no documented trans-specific criminal offence. The main traveller-facing exposure is detention. One documented case (March 2024) placed a trans foreign woman in a male-foreigner guarded centre, and medication was withheld for three months; intervention and a 2024 court ruling show remedies can work, but the placement and denial recur in the record. Recourse is weak: hate-crime law excludes gender identity, the goods-and-services provision was struck down in 2019, and the 2019 violence figure is stale. Hostility is real but largely event-scoped (2019 counter-protests, 2020 mass arrests) and official rhetoric is hostile. Counterweights are a documented trans-rights civil society, a Supreme Court non-binary discrimination ruling, and no universal facility or ID-check exposure. Overall: Elevated Risk.

entry_documents.exposure: No documented visitor-facing marker-mismatch refusals; visitors carry home-country passports; visa-free stays up to 90 days.
entry_documents.protection: Documented: no entry rule targeting trans visitors; no marker-based checkpoint screening found.
entry_documents.interaction: Documents usually come from home state, so resident gender-recognition procedures do not touch visitors; a mismatch could still trigger secondary screening, which is not documented.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: March 2024: a trans foreign woman was placed in a guarded centre for male foreigners; hormone therapy was interrupted for three months. Prison placement and medication denial were litigated and damages (EUR 8,000) awarded in July 2024.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Border commander ordered release after NGO intervention; the human-rights court ruling confirms medication denial is litigable.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Birth-sex-linked placement by a state agency, with remedy depending on NGO intervention and litigation rather than routine practice; the detention pathway is the key state-interaction exposure.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Prison and detention placement by birth sex documented in one case; medication supply refused by a guarded centre.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Court remedy available and has produced a damages award for a trans prisoner; no general facility ban documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Recourse is ex post and litigation-dependent; no evidence of a standing protocol for trans detainees.

care_services.exposure: Medication denial in detention documented; the 2024 damages case concerned prison authorities.
care_services.protection: Court-ordered compensation shows litigable access to hormone therapy in custody; no general clinic-refusal rule for visitors documented.
care_services.interaction: Care access for a detained visitor depends on detaining body cooperating; ordinary-clinic access for visitors is not documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Head of state's 2020 statement called LGBT 'an ideology more harmful than Communism'; 'LGBT-free zone' stickers; 11 discriminatory local acts remain in force (family-rights charters); 2007 proposal to punish promotion of homosexuality.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Most LGBT-free resolutions annulled by administrative courts; the last explicit one annulled February 2024; Supreme Court found non-binary gender discrimination in February 2025.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official hostility is rhetorical and local; national courts have repeatedly reversed exclusionary acts, though residual acts persist.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented for visitors with minors. Same-sex adoption is barred and school 'promotion' rules were proposed in 2007; no trans-minor custody or school exposure documented for visitors.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor's exposure would turn on school and medical contact, which is not covered by the record.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: July 2019 counter-protest violence (4,000 vs 800 marchers) and August 2020 mass arrests (47 people). Technology-facilitated gender-based violence online documented in a 2025 report. The 1-in-5 attack figure is a 2019 snapshot covering 2014-2019 and is not used.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Heavy riot police intervention in 2019; Ombudsman criticised the 2020 arrests; no trans-specific violence rate with a denominator.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Violence is event-scoped around marches; police response is mixed; no visitor-specific violence record.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Hate-crime and hate-speech law excludes gender identity; the 2025 amendments were unsigned or ruled unconstitutional; the discrimination-in-services provision was struck down in 2019; the hate-speech bill is pending.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Anti-discrimination coverage for sexual orientation in employment; the Supreme Court recognises non-binary gender discrimination; the civil-society infrastructure (trans foundation, campaigns) is documented.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Visitors have limited recourse for gender-identity bias in services or street hate; courts and civil-society complaints work for residents more than for visitors.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.45-B has documented health-ministry denial of gender-related care to nonresidents and segregated education. This dossier has a documented detention placement and medication denial, but no standing visitor care ban, so it sits slightly higher.

0.55-B has routine secondary screening, refused entry and humiliating searches. This dossier documents no routine border friction for trans visitors, but it has a detention placement case and no hate-crime recourse, so it is similar to 0.55-B.

0.65-A has a document-mismatch detention that was remedied and a national equality law operating. This dossier's remedies are less consistent (hate-crime law excludes gender identity), and the detention placement was documented as harmful, so it sits lower.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller-facing exposure is concentrated in detention. A single documented case placed a trans foreign woman in a male-foreigner centre and withheld hormone therapy for three months. Remedies worked only after NGO intervention and litigation, and a 2024 ruling confirmed that medication denial is litigable. Other exposures are event-scoped (2019 counter-protest violence, 2020 mass arrests) or rhetorical (official hostility), and no universal facility, ID-check or registration exposure is documented. Recourse is thin because hate-crime law excludes gender identity and the services-discrimination provision was struck down. Positives are documented: courts have repeatedly reversed anti-LGBT acts, and a Supreme Court ruling recognised non-binary gender discrimination. The result is Elevated Risk.
